translationRepairs: Li Dui, courtesy name Zixi, was a native of Linjing in Xu Prefecture.
Li Dui, courtesy name Zixi, was a native of Linying in Xu Prefecture.
臨潁 is Linying, not Linjing.
When Zhang Yaozhuo was assigned to Heyang, Dui argued that Yaozhuo had long lacked both character and competence and should not be appointed merely because he was an imperial in-law.
When Zhang Yaozuo was assigned to Heyang, Dui argued that Yaozuo had long lacked both character and competence and should not be appointed merely because he was an imperial in-law.
張堯佐 is romanized Zhang Yaozuo; 佐 is zuo, not zhuo.
Rising through the ranks to vice director of the right in the Ministry of Revenue, he was transferred to minister of works and retired.
Rising through the ranks to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, he was transferred to minister of works and retired.
尚書右丞 is the Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, not an office of the Ministry of Revenue.
He served as vice prefect of Yongxing Circuit, then as a Hanlin collator, and after four promotions was made Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengde Circuit.

He served as vice prefect of Yongxing Circuit, then as collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and after four promotions was made academician-expositor of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengde Circuit.
集賢校理 is a collator of the Jixian (Assembled Worthies) Hall and 龍圖閣直學士 is academician-expositor of the Longtu Pavilion; neither is a Hanlin post.
Zhang Dao, courtesy name Jingyuan, was the son of Zhang Kui, Hanlin academician-attendant at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Zhang Dao, courtesy name Jingyuan, was the son of Zhang Kui, academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
樞密直學士 is academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, not a Hanlin academician-attendant.

When the court planned to renovate the Mujin Residence and proposed seizing private homes, Dao said: "Fanglin Garden still has unused land, and the imperial clan have ample room — there is no need to tear down people's houses."

When the court planned to renovate the Muqin Residence and proposed seizing private homes, Dao said: "Fanglin Garden still has unused land, and the imperial clan have ample room — there is no need to tear down people's houses."
睦親宅 is romanized Muqin, not Mujin.

He served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Deng and Xu, again as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then as director of the Office for Memorials and Documents and superintendent of Chongfu Palace, and was promoted from Supervising Censor to Grandee of Manifest Counsel.

He served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Deng and Xu, again as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then as director of the Office for Memorials and Documents and superintendent of Chongfu Palace, and was promoted from Supervising Secretary to Grandee of Manifest Counsel.
給事中 is the Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not a Supervising Censor.
Liu Jin, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was a native of Ji Prefecture and the son of Liu Hong.
Liu Jin, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was a native of Ji Prefecture and the son of Liu Hang.
劉沆 is Liu Hang; 沆 is read hang, not hong.
When Hong died, Jin received posthumous honors on his father's behalf.
When Hang died, Jin received posthumous honors on his father's behalf.
沆 is read hang (Liu Hang), not hong.
He was summoned to compile the Veritable Records, made historiography compiler and Hebei transport commissioner, and appointed Hanlin attendant and prefect of Ying.

He was summoned to compile the Diaries of Activity and Repose, made historiography compiler and Hebei transport commissioner, and appointed academician-attendant of the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Ying.
起居注 are the Diaries of Activity and Repose, not the Veritable Records; 天章閣待制 is not a Hanlin post.
He was punished for corresponding with Wang Shiju and transferred to Ming Prefecture.
He was punished for corresponding with Zhao Shiju and transferred to Ming Prefecture.
世居 is the imperial clansman Zhao Shiju of the Xining 8 treason case; nothing in the text supports the surname Wang.
By accumulated rank he rose to Director of the Secretariat and Guest of the Heir Apparent.
By accumulated rank he rose to Director of the Palace Library and Guest of the Heir Apparent.
秘書監 is the Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.
The historians comment: Zuo and Li distinguished themselves in fiscal administration and won praise in their own day.
The historians comment: Zuo and Li distinguished themselves in water-control administration and won praise in their own day.
水衡之政 here refers to the river and water-conservancy work for which Yang Zuo and Shen Li are praised, not fiscal administration.
Dui counseled and remonstrated in office without parading his virtue; earlier generations had already embodied that same restraint.
Dui counseled and remonstrated in office without parading his virtue, and Xian was able to carry on that example.
先 is Li Xian, Li Dui's cousin whose notice follows Dui's, not 'earlier generations'.
At the start of the Xining era he was granted direct appointment to the Hall of Dragon Designs and made prefect of Guangzhou.
At the start of the Xining era he was made auxiliary academician of the Longtu Pavilion (Hall of Dragon Designs) and prefect of Guangzhou.
直龍圖閣 is the honorary title Auxiliary of the Longtu Pavilion; 直 is not 'direct appointment'.
He was granted direct appointment to the Historical Archives and made prefect of Chan Prefecture.
He was made auxiliary of the Historiography Institute and appointed prefect of Chan Prefecture.
直史館 is the title Auxiliary of the Historiography Institute; 直 is not 'direct appointment'.

He was again dispatched to the Chengdu circuit, then recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Household Department and appointed prefect of Hongzhou with the title Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent.
He was again dispatched to the Chengdu circuit, then recalled as Vice Commissioner of Revenue and appointed prefect of Hongzhou with the title Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
集賢殿修撰 is Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; 戶部副使 is Vice Commissioner of Revenue.
By accumulated rank he had risen to Director of the Secretariat; he was sixty-five.
By accumulated rank he had risen to Director of the Palace Library; he was sixty-five.
秘書監 is the Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.
He held the post of Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices and supervised the Xianyuan Monastery, then died at seventy-four.
He held the post of Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and supervised the Xianyuan Abbey, then died at seventy-four.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not an office for imperial sacrifices.
During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui dynasty, an ancestor named Jing Che, commended for putting down the Lu tribes, was made prefect of Puzhou. After his death his line settled there for good.
During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui dynasty, an ancestor named Jingche, commended for putting down the Lu tribes, was made prefect of Puzhou. After his death his line settled there for good.
景徹 is the given name of a Yao ancestor; 'Jing Che' wrongly splits it like a surname and given name.
He died in office as Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices at sixty-seven.
He died in office as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at sixty-seven.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
He was promoted again to Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices.
He was promoted again to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
After a year he was transferred to Luzhou and given the additional title of Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
After more than a year he was transferred to Luzhou and given the added title of Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
集賢院學士 is an Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, not a Hanlin post.

Called to the capital, he became Grand Director of the Office of Imperial Manufactories and Vice Minister of Revenue, then served as Pavilion Drafting Gentleman-at-Large in Hangzhou, Yongxing, Henan, and Yingzhou.

Called to the capital as Chief Minister of the Court of the Treasury, he rose to Vice Minister of Revenue, then as Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion governed Hangzhou, the Yongxing Army, Henan and Yingzhou.
太府卿 is Chief Minister of the Court of the Treasury; 寶文閣待制 is Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion.
Before long he retired with the rank of Grandee for Splendid Happiness.
Before long he retired as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not the Grandee for Splendid Happiness (光祿大夫).
He eventually reached the rank of Grandee for Splendid Happiness and died at seventy-seven.
He eventually rose to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and died at seventy-seven.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not the Grandee for Splendid Happiness (光祿大夫).
He served in turn as prefect of Guang, Qian, and Guo Prefectures, rose to Grandee for Splendid Happiness, and was promoted to Grandee for Miscellaneous Uses.
He served in turn as prefect of Guang, Qian and Guo Prefectures, held the office of Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was changed to Grandee of Palace Leisure.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; 中散大夫 is Grandee of Palace Leisure.

He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run Prefecture, then promoted to Grandee for Splendid Happiness and prefect of Xuan Prefecture, where his administration ranked first in Jiangdong.

He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run Prefecture, then promoted to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and prefect of Xuan Prefecture, where his administration ranked first in Jiangdong.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
He was promoted again to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, governed Jingnan and E Prefectures, and died at seventy.
He was promoted again to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, governed Jingnan and E Prefecture, and died at seventy.
光祿卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not the Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan.

Summoned to audience, his answers on affairs in Jiaozhi and Guangdong pleased the emperor. He was made bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, Hanlin attendant at the Zhaowen Pavilion, and again prefect of Gui Prefecture.

Summoned to audience, his answers on affairs in Jiaozhi and Guangnan pleased the emperor. He returned as Bureau Director of Honors, auxiliary of the Zhaowen Institute, and again prefect of Gui Prefecture.
司封郎中 is Bureau Director of Honors (Ministry of Personnel); 直昭文館 is an auxiliary of the Zhaowen Institute, not a Hanlin post.
Pan Su, courtesy name Bogong, was a collateral descendant of Prince Mei of Zheng.
Pan Su, courtesy name Bogong, was a grand-nephew of Pan Mei, Prince of Zheng.
從孫 is a grand-nephew; 鄭王美 is Pan Mei, posthumously Prince of Zheng.
